121	class DatasetCatalog:
122	    def __init__(self, path):
123	        self.path = Path(path)
124	
125	    def entries(self):
126	        return json.loads(self.path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) if self.path.exists() else {}
127	
128	    def _normalize_entry(self, dataset, known_ids):
129	        return _normalized_record(dataset, known_ids)
130	
131	    def register(self, dataset):
132	        records = self.entries()
133	        if not isinstance(dataset, dict):
134	            raise ValueError("invalid dataset descriptor")
135	        identifier = dataset.get("id")
136	        if not isinstance(identifier, str) or not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*", identifier):
137	            raise ValueError("invalid dataset id")
138	        if identifier in records:
139	            raise ValueError("dataset already registered")
140	        entry = self._normalize_entry(dataset, set(records))
141	        records[identifier] = entry
142	        self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
143	        self.path.write_text(json.dumps(records, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
144	        return entry
145	
146	    def describe(self, identifier):
147	        records = self.entries()
148	        if identifier not in records:
149	            raise ValueError("unknown dataset")
150	        return records[identifier]
151	
152	    def search(self, query="", field_type=None, tags=None, owner=None):
153	        if not isinstance(query, str):
154	            raise ValueError("query must be a string")
155	        if field_type is not None and field_type not in FIELD_TYPES:
156	            raise ValueError("field_type must be None or one of string, integer, number, boolean")
157	        required_tags = _normalize_tags(tags) if tags is not None else []
158	        required_owner = _normalize_owner(owner).casefold() if owner is not None else None
159	        words = {word.casefold() for word in query.split()}
160	        records = self.entries()
161	        results = []
162	        for identifier in sorted(records):
163	            entry = records[identifier]
164	            if field_type is not None and not any(field["type"] == field_type for field in entry["fields"]):
165	                continue
166	            if required_tags:
167	                available = {tag.casefold() for tag in entry.get("tags", [])}
168	                if not all(tag.casefold() in available for tag in required_tags):
169	                    continue
170	            if required_owner is not None:
171	                entry_owner = entry.get("owner")
172	                if not isinstance(entry_owner, str) or entry_owner.casefold() != required_owner:
173	                    continue
174	            matched_indices = set()
175	            matched = True
176	            dataset_haystack = (entry["id"] + "\n" + entry.get("description", "")).casefold()
177	            for word in words:
178	                hits = {index for index, field in enumerate(entry["fields"])
179	                        if word in field["name"].casefold()}
180	                matched_indices.update(hits)
181	                if not hits and word not in dataset_haystack:
182	                    matched = False
183	                    break
184	            if matched:
185	                results.append({"dataset": entry,
186	                                "matched_fields": [entry["fields"][index]["name"]
187	                                                   for index in sorted(matched_indices)]})
188	        return results
189	
190	    def dependencies(self, identifier):
191	        entry = self.describe(identifier)
192	        return [self.describe(key) for key in entry["depends_on"]]
193	
194	    def impact(self, identifier, max_depth=None):
195	        if max_depth is not None and (isinstance(max_depth, bool)
196	                                      or not isinstance(max_depth, int) or max_depth <= 0):
197	            raise ValueError("max_depth must be None or a positive integer")
198	        records = self.entries()
199	        if identifier not in records:
200	            raise ValueError("unknown dataset")
201	        downstream = {}
202	        for key, entry in records.items():
203	            for source in entry["depends_on"]:
204	                downstream.setdefault(source, set()).add(key)
205	        reached = {identifier: [identifier]}
206	        frontier = {identifier: [identifier]}
207	        result = []
208	        distance = 0
209	        while frontier and (max_depth is None or distance < max_depth):
210	            distance += 1
211	            candidates = {}
212	            for node, path in frontier.items():
213	                for child in downstream.get(node, ()):  # unconnected records are never reached
214	                    if child in reached:
215	                        continue
216	                    candidate = path + [child]
217	                    if child not in candidates or candidate < candidates[child]:
218	                        candidates[child] = candidate
219	            if not candidates:
220	                break
221	            frontier = candidates
222	            reached.update(candidates)
223	            for child, path in candidates.items():
224	                result.append({"dataset": records[child], "distance": distance, "path": path})
225	        result.sort(key=lambda item: (item["distance"], item["dataset"]["id"]))
226	        return result
227	
228	    def export(self, identifiers=None):
229	        if identifiers is not None and not isinstance(identifiers, list):
230	            raise ValueError("identifiers must be None or a list of dataset ids")
231	        selected = []
232	        if identifiers is not None:
233	            for item in identifiers:
234	                if not isinstance(item, str) or not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*", item):
235	                    raise ValueError("invalid dataset id")
236	                if item not in selected:
237	                    selected.append(item)
238	        records = self.entries()
239	        unknown = [item for item in selected if item not in records]
240	        if unknown:
241	            raise ValueError("unknown dataset")
242	        if identifiers is None:
243	            selected = list(records)
244	
245	        included = set()
246	        stack = list(selected)
247	        while stack:
248	            key = stack.pop()
249	            if key in included:
250	                continue
251	            included.add(key)
252	            for source in records[key]["depends_on"]:
253	                if source not in records:
254	                    raise ValueError("missing dependency")
255	                if source not in included:
256	                    stack.append(source)
257	
258	        subset = {key: records[key] for key in included}
259	        ordered = _toposort(subset)
260	        if ordered is None:
261	            raise ValueError("dependency cycle detected")
262	        return {"datasets": [records[key] for key in ordered]}
263	
264	    def import_bundle(self, bundle):
265	        if not isinstance(bundle, dict):
266	            raise ValueError("bundle must be an object")
267	        descriptors = bundle.get("datasets")
268	        if not isinstance(descriptors, list):
269	            raise ValueError("bundle must contain a datasets array")
270	
271	        records = self.entries()
272	        batch_ids = set()
273	        for dataset in descriptors:
274	            if not isinstance(dataset, dict):
275	                raise ValueError("invalid dataset descriptor")
276	            identifier = dataset.get("id")
277	            if not isinstance(identifier, str) or not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*", identifier):
278	                raise ValueError("invalid dataset id")
279	            if identifier in records or identifier in batch_ids:
280	                raise ValueError("dataset already registered")
281	            batch_ids.add(identifier)
282	
283	        known = set(records) | batch_ids
284	        new_entries = {}
285	        for dataset in descriptors:
286	            entry = self._normalize_entry(dataset, known)
287	            if entry["id"] in entry["depends_on"]:
288	                raise ValueError("dependencies must be unique, already registered dataset ids")
289	            new_entries[entry["id"]] = entry
290	
291	        batch = {key: {"depends_on": [dep for dep in entry["depends_on"] if dep in batch_ids]}
292	                 for key, entry in new_entries.items()}
293	        ordered = _toposort(batch)
294	        if ordered is None:
295	            raise ValueError("dependency cycle detected")
296	
297	        imported = [new_entries[key] for key in ordered]
298	        if new_entries:
299	            for entry in imported:
300	                records[entry["id"]] = entry
301	            self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
302	            self.path.write_text(json.dumps(records, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n",
303	                                 encoding="utf-8")
304	        return {"datasets": imported}
305	
306	    def _snapshot_state(self, bundle):
307	        if not isinstance(bundle, dict):
308	            raise ValueError("bundle must be an object")
309	        descriptors = bundle.get("datasets")
310	        if not isinstance(descriptors, list):
311	            raise ValueError("bundle must contain a datasets array")
312	
313	        snapshot_ids = set()
314	        for dataset in descriptors:
315	            if not isinstance(dataset, dict):
316	                raise ValueError("invalid dataset descriptor")
317	            identifier = dataset.get("id")
318	            if not isinstance(identifier, str) or not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*", identifier):
319	                raise ValueError("invalid dataset id")
320	            if identifier in snapshot_ids:
321	                raise ValueError("dataset already registered")
322	            snapshot_ids.add(identifier)
323	
324	        snapshot = {}
325	        for dataset in descriptors:
326	            entry = _normalized_record(dataset, snapshot_ids)
327	            if entry["id"] in entry["depends_on"]:
328	                raise ValueError("dependencies must be unique, already registered dataset ids")
329	            snapshot[entry["id"]] = entry
330	        if _toposort(snapshot) is None:
331	            raise ValueError("dependency cycle detected")
332	        return snapshot
333	
334	    @staticmethod
335	    def _diff_states(current, snapshot):
336	        before_ids = set(current)
337	        after_ids = set(snapshot)
338	        added = [copy.deepcopy(snapshot[key]) for key in sorted(after_ids - before_ids)]
339	        removed = [copy.deepcopy(current[key]) for key in sorted(before_ids - after_ids)]
340	        changed = []
341	        for key in sorted(before_ids & after_ids):
342	            before = current[key]
343	            after = snapshot[key]
344	            changed_keys = sorted(name for name in set(before) | set(after)
345	                                  if before.get(name) != after.get(name))
346	            if changed_keys:
347	                changed.append({"id": key, "before": copy.deepcopy(before),
348	                                "after": copy.deepcopy(after), "changed_keys": changed_keys})
349	        return {"added": added, "removed": removed, "changed": changed}
350	
351	    def diff_bundle(self, bundle):
352	        snapshot = self._snapshot_state(bundle)
353	        records = self.entries()
354	        current = {key: _normalized_record(entry, set(records))
355	                   for key, entry in records.items()}
356	        return self._diff_states(current, snapshot)
357	
358	    def preview_bundle(self, bundle):
359	        snapshot = self._snapshot_state(bundle)
360	        records = self.entries()
361	        if not isinstance(records, dict):
362	            raise ValueError("invalid catalog state")
363	        current = {}
364	        for key, entry in records.items():
365	            normalized = _normalized_record(entry, set(records))
366	            if normalized["id"] != key:
367	                raise ValueError("invalid dataset descriptor")
368	            if normalized["id"] in normalized["depends_on"]:
369	                raise ValueError("dependencies must be unique, already registered dataset ids")
370	            current[key] = normalized
371	        if _toposort(current) is None:
372	            raise ValueError("dependency cycle detected")
373	
374	        diff = self._diff_states(current, snapshot)
375	        sources = {row["id"] for row in diff["added"]}
376	        sources.update(row["id"] for row in diff["removed"])
377	        sources.update(row["id"] for row in diff["changed"])
378	
379	        # target id -> source id -> {"before"/"after": propagation explanation}
380	        reached_by = {}
381	        for side, state in (("before", current), ("after", snapshot)):
382	            downstream = _downstream_index(state)
383	            for source in sources:
384	                if source not in state:
385	                    continue
386	                for target, path in _shortest_downstream_paths(downstream, source).items():
387	                    propagation = {"distance": len(path) - 1, "path": path}
388	                    reached_by.setdefault(target, {}).setdefault(source, {})[side] = propagation
389	
390	        affected = []
391	        for target in sorted(reached_by):
392	            causes = []
393	            for source in sorted(reached_by[target]):
394	                sides = reached_by[target][source]
395	                before = sides.get("before")
396	                after = sides.get("after")
397	                if before is None and after is None:
398	                    continue
399	                causes.append({"id": source, "before": before, "after": after})
400	            if causes:
401	                affected.append({"id": target, "causes": causes})
402	        return {"diff": diff, "affected": affected}

import json
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
from dataset_catalog import DatasetCatalog

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent


class CatalogTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.temp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT)
        self.addCleanup(self.temp.cleanup)
        self.path = Path(self.temp.name) / "catalog.json"
        self.catalog = DatasetCatalog(self.path)
        self.raw = {"id": "orders", "fields": [{"name": "amount", "type": "number"}]}

    def test_register_persists_schema_and_direct_dependencies(self):
        self.catalog.register(self.raw)
        self.catalog.register({"id": "daily", "fields": [{"name": "total", "type": "number"}], "depends_on": ["orders"]})
        self.catalog.register({"id": "weekly", "fields": [{"name": "total", "type": "number"}], "depends_on": ["daily"]})
        fresh = DatasetCatalog(self.path)
        self.assertEqual([row["id"] for row in fresh.dependencies("weekly")], ["daily"])
        self.assertEqual(fresh.describe("orders")["fields"], self.raw["fields"])

    def test_bad_dependencies_and_duplicate_fields_do_not_write(self):
        for item in ({**self.raw, "depends_on": ["unknown"]}, {**self.raw, "fields": self.raw["fields"] * 2}):
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                self.catalog.register(item)
        self.assertFalse(self.path.exists())

    def test_duplicate_and_unknown_dataset(self):
        self.catalog.register(self.raw)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.catalog.register(self.raw)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.catalog.dependencies("missing")

    def _register(self, identifier, depends_on=None):
        self.catalog.register({"id": identifier,
                               "fields": [{"name": "n", "type": "integer"}],
                               "depends_on": depends_on or []})

    def test_impact_lists_reachable_downstream_with_shortest_paths(self):
        for identifier, depends_on in (("orders", []), ("daily", ["orders"]),
                                       ("weekly", ["daily"]), ("report", ["orders"])):
            self._register(identifier, depends_on)
        result = self.catalog.impact("orders")
        self.assertEqual([(row["dataset"]["id"], row["distance"], row["path"]) for row in result],
                         [("daily", 1, ["orders", "daily"]),
                          ("report", 1, ["orders", "report"]),
                          ("weekly", 2, ["orders", "daily", "weekly"])])

    def test_impact_respects_max_depth_and_empty_leaf(self):
        for identifier, depends_on in (("orders", []), ("daily", ["orders"]),
                                       ("weekly", ["daily"])):
            self._register(identifier, depends_on)
        self.assertEqual([row["dataset"]["id"] for row in self.catalog.impact("orders", 1)], ["daily"])
        self.assertEqual(self.catalog.impact("weekly"), [])

    def test_impact_picks_lexicographically_smallest_shortest_path(self):
        for identifier, depends_on in (("orders", []), ("b", ["orders"]), ("c", ["orders"]),
                                       ("d", ["c", "b"])):
            self._register(identifier, depends_on)
        result = self.catalog.impact("orders")
        self.assertEqual([row["dataset"]["id"] for row in result], ["b", "c", "d"])
        self.assertEqual(result[-1]["path"], ["orders", "b", "d"])

    def test_impact_rejects_invalid_max_depth_and_unknown_source(self):
        self._register("orders")
        for bad in (True, False, 0, -1, 1.0, "1"):
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                self.catalog.impact("orders", bad)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.catalog.impact("missing")

    def test_cli_impact(self):
        prefix = [sys.executable, str(ROOT / "dataset_catalog.py"), "--catalog", str(self.path)]
        subprocess.run(prefix + ["register", str(ROOT / "samples/orders.json")], check=True, capture_output=True)
        subprocess.run(prefix + ["register", str(ROOT / "samples/daily.json")], check=True, capture_output=True)
        ok = subprocess.run(prefix + ["impact", "orders"], capture_output=True, text=True)
        self.assertEqual(ok.returncode, 0, ok.stderr)
        result = json.loads(ok.stdout)
        self.assertEqual([row["dataset"]["id"] for row in result], ["daily_totals"])
        self.assertEqual(result[0]["distance"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(result[0]["path"], ["orders", "daily_totals"])
        self.assertEqual(subprocess.run(prefix + ["impact", "orders", "--max-depth", "0"],
                                       capture_output=True, text=True).returncode, 2)
        depth_error = subprocess.run(prefix + ["impact", "missing", "--max-depth", "x"],
                                     capture_output=True, text=True)
        self.assertEqual(depth_error.returncode, 2)
        self.assertIn("error", json.loads(depth_error.stdout))
        self.assertEqual(subprocess.run(prefix + ["impact", "missing"],
                                        capture_output=True).returncode, 2)

    def test_cli_query_and_registration(self):
        prefix = [sys.executable, str(ROOT / "dataset_catalog.py"), "--catalog", str(self.path)]
        run = subprocess.run(prefix + ["register", str(ROOT / "samples/orders.json")], capture_output=True, text=True)
        self.assertEqual(run.returncode, 0, run.stderr)
        query = subprocess.run(prefix + ["describe", "orders"], capture_output=True, text=True)
        self.assertEqual(json.loads(query.stdout)["id"], "orders")
        self.assertEqual(subprocess.run(prefix + ["describe", "missing"], capture_output=True).returncode, 2)

    def _chain(self):
        for identifier, depends_on in (("orders", []), ("daily_totals", ["orders"]),
                                       ("weekly", ["daily_totals"]), ("report", ["orders"])):
            self._register(identifier, depends_on)

    def test_export_all_orders_dependencies_before_dependents(self):
        self._chain()
        result = self.catalog.export()
        self.assertEqual(set(result), {"datasets"})
        ids = [row["id"] for row in result["datasets"]]
        self.assertEqual(ids.index("orders"), 0)
        self.assertLess(ids.index("daily_totals"), ids.index("weekly"))
        self.assertEqual([row["id"] for row in self.catalog.export([])["datasets"]], [])

    def test_export_selected_includes_only_upstream_closure(self):
        self._chain()
        ids = [row["id"] for row in self.catalog.export(["daily_totals"])["datasets"]]
        self.assertEqual(ids, ["orders", "daily_totals"])
        self.assertEqual([row["id"] for row in self.catalog.export(["orders"])["datasets"]], ["orders"])
        ids = [row["id"] for row in self.catalog.export(["report", "weekly", "weekly"])["datasets"]]
        self.assertEqual(ids, ["orders", "daily_totals", "report", "weekly"])
        ids = [row["id"] for row in self.catalog.export(["weekly", "report"])["datasets"]]
        self.assertEqual(ids, ["orders", "daily_totals", "report", "weekly"])
        daily = self.catalog.describe("daily_totals")
        self.assertEqual(self.catalog.export(["daily_totals"])["datasets"][1], daily)
        self.assertEqual(list(self.catalog.export(["daily_totals"])["datasets"][1]),
                         ["id", "description", "fields", "depends_on"])

    def test_export_rejects_bad_arguments_and_unknown_ids(self):
        self._register("orders")
        for bad in ("orders", ("orders",), {1}, True, 1):
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                self.catalog.export(bad)
        for bad in ([""], ["Orders"], ["ord ers"], [1], [None], ["orders", ""]):
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                self.catalog.export(bad)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.catalog.export(["missing"])

    def _write_records(self, records):
        self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.path.write_text(json.dumps(records), encoding="utf-8")

    def test_search_matches_keywords_across_id_description_and_field_names(self):
        self._write_records({
            "orders": {"id": "orders", "description": "Order amounts from the daily export",
                       "fields": [{"name": "order_id", "type": "string"},
                                  {"name": "amount", "type": "number"}], "depends_on": []},
            "daily_totals": {"id": "daily_totals", "description": "Daily totals derived from orders",
                             "fields": [{"name": "day", "type": "string"},
                                        {"name": "total", "type": "number"}],

    def _snapshot_record(self, identifier, depends_on=None, tags=..., description=...,
                         fields=None):
        record = {"id": identifier,
                  "description": identifier + " desc" if description is ... else description,
                  "fields": fields or [{"name": "n", "type": "integer"}],
                  "depends_on": depends_on or []}
        if tags is not ... and tags is not None:
            record["tags"] = tags
        return record

    def test_preview_diff_matches_diff_bundle_and_structure(self):
        self.catalog.import_bundle({"datasets": [
            self._snapshot_record("a"), self._snapshot_record("b", ["a"])]})
        bundle = {"datasets": [
            self._snapshot_record("a", description="updated"),
            self._snapshot_record("b", ["a"]), self._snapshot_record("c", ["b"])]}
        result = self.catalog.preview_bundle(bundle)
        self.assertEqual(set(result), {"diff", "affected"})
        self.assertEqual(result["diff"], self.catalog.diff_bundle(bundle))
        self.assertEqual([item["id"] for item in result["affected"]], ["b", "c"])
        b, c = result["affected"]
        self.assertEqual(set(b), {"id", "causes"})
        self.assertEqual(set(c), {"id", "causes"})
        self.assertEqual(b["causes"], [
            {"id": "a", "before": {"distance": 1, "path": ["a", "b"]},
             "after": {"distance": 1, "path": ["a", "b"]}}])
        self.assertEqual(c["causes"], [
            {"id": "a", "before": None,
             "after": {"distance": 2, "path": ["a", "b", "c"]}}])
        for item in result["affected"]:
            for cause in item["causes"]:
                self.assertEqual(set(cause), {"id", "before", "after"})
                for side in ("before", "after"):
                    if cause[side] is not None:
                        self.assertEqual(set(cause[side]), {"distance", "path"})

def test_apply_replaces_adds_removes_and_returns_pre_commit_diff(self):
        self.catalog.import_bundle({"datasets": [
            self._snapshot_record("a"), self._snapshot_record("b", ["a"]),
            self._snapshot_record("c", ["b"])]})
        bundle = {"datasets": [
            self._snapshot_record("a", description="updated"),
            self._snapshot_record("b", ["a"]),
            self._snapshot_record("d", ["a", "b"])]}
        diff_before = self.catalog.diff_bundle(bundle)
        result = self.catalog.apply_bundle(bundle)
        self.assertEqual(result, diff_before)
        self.assertEqual(set(result), {"added", "removed", "changed"})
        self.assertEqual([row["id"] for row in result["added"]], ["d"])
        self.assertEqual([row["id"] for row in result["removed"]], ["c"])
        self.assertEqual([row["id"] for row in result["changed"]], ["a"])
        self.assertEqual(result["changed"][0]["before"]["description"], "a desc")
        self.assertEqual(result["changed"][0]["after"]["description"], "updated")

        fresh = DatasetCatalog(self.path)

content.text:
Done. All 83 tests pass (67 pre-existing + 16 new) under Python 3.10 with no new dependencies.

## Changes

**`dataset_catalog.py`**
- Added `DatasetCatalog.apply_bundle(bundle)`:
  - Validates the snapshot with the existing `_snapshot_state` (non-object, missing/non-array `datasets`, bad descriptors, duplicate ids, duplicate/missing/self dependencies, cycles all raise `ValueError`; forward references allowed only inside the snapshot) and validates the current catalog with `preview`'s rules via a new extracted `_current_state()` helper — missing file or `{`}` means empty.
  - Returns the same `{"added", "removed", "changed"}` a pre-commit `diff_bundle` would produce — ids sorted, `changed_keys` sorted, full deep-copied before/after records — so same-id replacement, new-id addition, snapshot-omitted removal, partial export = full target, and `[]` = clear all hold.
  - All-or-nothing commit: any validation failure happens before writing, so the original file is untouched and missing files/parents are never created; an empty diff writes nothing and creates no directories. On a real diff it serializes all normalized records in the existing storage format, creates parent directories, and saves via a sibling temp file + `os.replace`, so a save failure raises `OSError` with the original contents intact (and a previously missing file still absent).
  - Never mutates the input; returned records are copies. Queries and `export` reflect the new state immediately.
- Added the `apply FILE` subparser and CLI dispatch: same JSON to stdout, exit 0 on success; unreadable file, bad JSON, validation or save failure print `{"error": ...}` and exit 2 (already covered by the existing exception handler).

**`README.md`** — documented the CLI `apply FILE` command and `DatasetCatalog.apply_bundle` API alongside `diff`/`preview`.

**`test_dataset_catalog.py`** — added tests for replace/add/remove diff parity with `diff_bundle`, partial-export and empty-array clearing, no-write no-op (including input ordering), missing-catalog parent creation, `{}` empty state, normalization (description/fields/tags/owner/extra-key dropping), snapshot + current-catalog validation rejection without writing, non-mutation of input and returned records, `OSError` atomicity (original file intact, temp file cleaned up via mocked `os.replace`), and CLI success/no-op/error paths including catalog creation.

`register`/`import` append semantics and `diff`/`preview` read-only behavior are unchanged — `preview_bundle` now simply shares the extracted `_current_state()` validation.
